cause.label: equity_offering
cause.what_happened: At 16:28 ET on 2026-09-22 Voyager launched a $350m (+$52.5m option) convertible senior notes offering due 2032, about 18% of market cap, with a capped call and no concurrent buyback or prepaid forward. The stock fell about 7% after hours, gapped -11.8%, and lost another 8.3% during today's marketing session, when convert arbitrage funds put on their hedge shorts. Morgan Stanley also cut its target to $37 (Underweight) on 09-22.

pipeline.next_dated_event: Pricing release for the 2032 convertible notes, expected after today's close or before the 2026-09-24 open. The date is inferred from the 2025 deal's one-day marketing (launch 2025-11-05, priced off the 11-06 close); the company has not announced one.
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: A large upsize (the 2025 deal went from $300m to $435m) or a low conversion premium in the pricing release. Either one would mean more hedge supply or a distressed read and would turn this negative. So would the deal failing to price tonight, which leaves the arb short supply open through 09-24.

findings.finding: The selling that set today's intraday price is convertible-arbitrage hedge shorting against a $350m note deal launched 2026-09-22 at 16:28 ET. It ends at pricing, which on the issuer's own precedent lands after today's close and is announced before the 2026-09-24 open. That release also triggers the capped-call counterparties' initial hedge purchases, which the launch release itself says could raise the share price. Sized net of the risk that the release carries an upsize.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The pricing press release for the 2032 notes. The 2025 deal was launched 2025-11-05, marketed one day, priced off the 2025-11-06 close, and the pricing was released 2025-11-07. The same cadence puts this pricing on today's close and the release before the 09-24 open. The release fixes the hedge ratio (arb shorting is done), and the launch release states that capped-call counterparties 'expect to enter into various derivative transactions ... and/or purchase shares' concurrently with or shortly after pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior instance, the Nov 2025 convertible. Marketing day 2025-11-06: -9.4% (26.29 to 23.83). Day after pricing, 2025-11-07: opened 23.15 (-2.9%) and closed 23.45 (-1.6%), and the stock kept drifting to 20.92 by 11-13. That deal was upsized 45% at pricing and came with a $175m repurchase and prepaid forward (launch release). This one has neither, so today's hedge shorting had to go through the open market, which is consistent with the deeper -19% fall against -9.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Today's tape holds the arbs' short supply while the deal size and terms are still open. It does not hold the end of that supply or the capped-call dealers' purchases, which only start at pricing. If the market already priced the deal as done, the intraday leg would have been flat after the gap instead of adding another 8.3%. The upsize risk, which the 2025 precedent shows, cuts the other way and is netted into the +0.8.
findings.independence: Mechanism timing: the issuer's own 2025 launch/pricing pair on EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788060/000162828025051764/ex991launchpressrelease.htm and https://voyagertechnologies.com/press-releases/voyager-technologies-inc-prices-upsized-435-0-million-convertible-senior-notes-offering/). Direction: the same precedent points AGAINST a bounce (-1.6% the day after pricing), so the independent evidence on sign is contrary.

baseline_tension: The finding leans positive (supply ends at pricing). It cuts against this stock's own day-after-pricing in Nov 2025 (-1.6%), its comparable falls (median -2.04%, 1 of 3 up) and its high 8.7% ATR. It agrees with the modest 5x volume (no 15x capitulation signature) and the -25..-15 cross-section band (+0.27%). So expected_move is cut from the +0.8 finding sum to +0.2, a reduction of 0.6.
